description:
FILED s450u (Opus, round 8 agent U) while shipping #560.

#560 memoized `_extract_module_prototypes` on disk (Pl::ProtoCache, one entry
per MODULE).  Its sibling `_extract_file_prototypes` -- the walk for a
path-required file, `require './test.pl'` -- is still memoized per PROCESS
only, and it is the walk every perl-tests file pays: `perl-tests/t/test.pl`
is ~1 200 lines and is walked once in each of the 108 sweep processes, plus
once per gate row that transpiles a perl-tests file.

MEASURE FIRST (the discriminating measurement, not taken here because #560's
bar was the emission A/B): time `pl2cl` on a two-line program that does
`require './perl-tests/t/test.pl'` against one that does not.  If the
difference is small the task is not worth doing; the A/B over 30 perl-tests
files in s450u showed no cache win at all (12.6 s both sides), which is
consistent with either "test.pl is cheap" or "the win is there but the
modules those files use are already skipped by name".

IF IT IS WORTH DOING, the shape is #560's exactly, and Pl::ProtoCache was
written so this is a small change: the entry key becomes the file's ABSOLUTE
path + mtime + size + generation + compiler stamp (the resolution is already
done by the caller -- `_extract_file_prototypes` resolves ./NAME against the
cwd, the requiring file's dir and its ancestors, so the ABS path is the only
identity), and the dependency list + cycle/inc-path taint machinery is
already in place and already tracks file walks (`note_dep('file', ...)`).
The reason it was not cached in s450u is scope: the s449 ruling pins the
cache family to "ONE ENTRY PER MODULE", and a path-required file is not a
module -- the same bytes reached through two different requiring files are
the same entry, which is right, but it wanted a ruling rather than an
assumption.
subject: _extract_file_prototypes (the `require './test.pl'` walk) is still memoized PER PROCESS -- #560's shape applies, but MEASURE the cost first
